title: Why Distributed Systems Fail
subtitle: Systems rarely fail all at once; they degrade along specific edges, cohorts and paths

panels.heading: Aggregate Looks Fine
panels.caption: The overall success rate stays high while one path quietly degrades
panels.note: A single global success rate hides partial failure by definition

panels.heading: One Edge Is Broken
panels.caption: A hot shard, one zone or a saturated pool fails a subset of requests
panels.note: Asymmetric symptoms: clients see timeouts while the server sees healthy traffic

panels.heading: Contain the Edge
panels.caption: Bounded waiting and per-edge controls keep one failure from spreading
panels.note: Budgeted retries with jitter, per-host breakers and readiness gates for brownouts

strip_title: Design for the dominant failure mode
strip_caption: Put identity, budgets and control at every hop, then rehearse with targeted fault drills
